Simulate the ODYSSEY LONG TERM trial

Source: R/odyssey-lt.R
simulate_odyssey_lt.Rd

Returns simulated, analysis-ready LDL cholesterol data modelled on ODYSSEY LONG TERM, a trial of alirocumab against placebo (NCT01507831). Every subject is made up. The data has one row per subject per scheduled visit, with no missing values, ready for the trial's mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM).

Usage

simulate_odyssey_lt(n)

Arguments

n

Number of subjects, at least 3, so that both arms get at least one subject. Subjects are randomized 2:1; when n is not a multiple of 3, the extra subjects get alirocumab. ODYSSEY LONG TERM randomized 2,341.

Value

A tibble with one row per subject per visit, sorted by subject and then visit. Columns that aren't numeric are factors:

  • subject_id: Subject identifier, such as "001-0001".

  • treatment: "Placebo" or "Alirocumab", with placebo as the reference level.

  • age: Age in years.

  • sex: "Female" or "Male".

  • race: "Black", "Other" or "White".

  • visit: Ordered factor, "Week 4" to "Week 52". LDL was also measured at Weeks 64 and 78, but the trial's primary model stops at Week 52.

  • day: Nominal study day of the visit, seven times the week.

  • ldl_baseline: LDL at baseline, in mg/dL.

  • ldl: LDL at the visit, in mg/dL.

  • ldl_pct_change: Percent change in LDL from baseline.

The last four columns are the randomization strata, which the trial's analysis plan adjusts for:

  • hefh: Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, "No" or "Yes".

  • prior_mi_stroke: Prior heart attack or ischemic stroke, "No" or "Yes".

  • statin_intensity: "High" or "Low/moderate".

  • region: "Eastern Europe", "North America", "Rest of World" or "Western Europe".

Details

The baseline LDL, the mean percent change at each visit, the demographics and the randomization strata follow the trial's published results. vignette("odyssey-lt", package = "clinique") explains each number, its source and the assumptions.

The data is simulated. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the trial's sponsors.

Reproducibility

Call set.seed() first to get the same data each time. The same seed gives the same data on every operating system. The correlated values at each visit are drawn with base R's chol(), which returns the one upper-triangular Cholesky factor of the covariance matrix. Methods based on eigen(), such as MASS::mvrnorm(), can return different factors on different systems, and so different data for the same seed.

References

FDA statistical review: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125559Orig1s000StatR.pdf

Robinson JG, et al. Efficacy and Safety of Alirocumab in Reducing Lipids and Cardiovascular Events. N Engl J Med 2015;372:1489-1499. Its statistical analysis plan is in the protocol supplement. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1501031

Examples

set.seed(1)
odyssey <- simulate_odyssey_lt(90)
head(odyssey)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 14
#>   subject_id treatment   age sex   race  visit   day ldl_baseline   ldl
#>   <fct>      <fct>     <dbl> <fct> <fct> <ord> <dbl>        <dbl> <dbl>

#> 2 001-0001   Alirocum…    42 Fema… Other Week…    56         66.8  15.9
#> 3 001-0001   Alirocum…    42 Fema… Other Week…    84         66.8  19.9
#> 4 001-0001   Alirocum…    42 Fema… Other Week…   112         66.8  11.4
#> 5 001-0001   Alirocum…    42 Fema… Other Week…   168         66.8  24.0
#> 6 001-0001   Alirocum…    42 Fema… Other Week…   252         66.8  31.8
